A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReTabAD benchmark and zero-shot LLM framework. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection experiments across 20 datasets, metadata ablations, feature-attribution evaluations, and reasoning-text experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, granular metadata ablations, broader attribution results, and detection F1 scores.

M1.justification: The metadata-conditioned prompting, record serialization, and structured anomaly-score, feature, and explanation outputs remain unchanged. Types E–G are experimental ablations. Corrected percentile labels in prompt examples agree with the 5th/95th-percentile procedure already documented in v1 Appendix D.2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 20 datasets and anomaly-detection tasks. Appendix A expands the domain descriptions, and Table 8 specifies glass class identifiers, without adding datasets or changing the stated class mapping.

E2.justification: Tables 13–14 add evaluated ICL, NPT-AD, and DisentAD baselines while retaining the previous comparators. Table 3 also includes the No Desc variant in the main cross-method comparison, using results previously reported in the ablation appendix.

E3.justification: Appendix K adds detection F1 with a threshold chosen to match the true test-set anomaly count. Appendix I adds metadata controls, retaining feature names in Types F/G. Table 7 revises feature and class counts, and Appendix A removes the approximately balanced test-set description. The principal 50%-normal training split remains unchanged; these revisions do not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices I–J add feature-only, domain-only, and statistics-plus-domain ablations across all five LLMs and 20 datasets, substantially expanding tests of individual metadata contributions. Table 15 extends SHAP-based feature-alignment analysis from Gemini to all five LLMs. The earlier reasoning-example experiment is retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state five runs with different seeds and report standard deviations in Appendices E–F. Added baseline columns follow the existing reporting practice. No increased run count, new confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Tables 13–14 add baseline results and revise existing values; for example, REPEN's wine AUROC changes from 0.657 to 0.472. Tables 15–19 add attribution, granular-ablation, and detection-F1 results. Gemini's headline average AUROC remains 0.847, and Table 3's No Desc scores already appeared in v1 Table 11. Revised appendix scores introduce some disagreements with the unchanged main-table values.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 replaces the conditional-density modeling objective p(x|M) with a general metadata-aware anomaly-scoring function f(x, M), removing the density-modeling formulation. This is a limited formal-definition revision; no theorem or proof is added, and Appendix G's alignment equations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction expands the stated algorithm coverage from 17 to 20. The principal contributions remain the same: 20 datasets with restored semantics, a competitive zero-shot framework, and evidence that metadata benefits detection and interpretation.

C2.justification: Appendix I adds a metadata-hierarchy interpretation and acknowledges that retained feature names prevent a pure domain-only ablation. Appendix G now distinguishes SHAP alignment from definitive explanation quality, while Appendix L discusses domain familiarity and metadata privacy. The earlier automobile small-sample caution is removed; the healthcare ethics discussion is relocated rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: Table 10 supplies hyperparameter ranges for the three added baselines. Appendix A specifies dataset-exclusion thresholds and clarifies deterministic label mapping; Table 8 adds glass class identifiers. Appendix D corrects prompt examples and clarifies configuration information. These documentation additions do not demonstrate changes to the existing method or resource availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussions and citations for ICL, NPT-AD, and DisentAD, plus McDermott et al. and DAGMM to motivate metric evaluation. Table 1 also corrects descriptions of existing resources. The central positioning around restoring semantic context remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites of the problem setup, dataset documentation, and attribution discussion, along with terminology and typographical corrections. The ethics statement moves after the conclusion, and appendices I–M are added. The existing main narrative and section order remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Visual reporting expands substantially: Tables 13–14 gain baseline columns, Table 15 expands from one LLM to five, and Tables 16–19 are added. Table 3 gains a No Desc column, Table 10 gains configurations, and several captions and prompt displays are corrected. The principal explanatory figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The finer metadata controls and broader attribution checks make the central semantic-context claims more testable, while Appendix G appropriately limits claims about explanation quality. These gains are tempered by reporting inconsistencies: v2 gives SLAD's vertebral AUROC as 0.679 in Table 3 but 0.600 in Table 13, and Appendix I's claim of consistent gains from adding feature descriptions conflicts with Claude's Table 16 results. The revision provides a modest net improvement rather than a substantial resolution of the paper's weaknesses.
